content:
Apple is turning 50, and plenty of its customers are even older. Apple recently launched a new support page listing 50 ways to make its devices easier to use, mostly through accessibility settings.

From adjusting font size on your Apple Watch to getting a notification on your iPhone when the washing machine cycle finishes, there's something for everyone…

Apple says its goal is to make technology work for everyone, including older users.

Apple believes the best technology should serve everyone, including older users. That's why our products and services are designed from the ground up with built-in accessibility features to help you stay connected, get creative, and do what you love — in whatever way works best for you. As life takes you through different stages, the way we interact with the world changes too. From enlarging onscreen text to making conversations clearer in a noisy restaurant, Apple's ecosystem of devices, features, and services is designed to adapt to your needs.

The support page mainly lists accessibility features, organised into ten categories.

  • Vision: View your screen comfortably
  • Hearing: Stay connected to conversations, alerts, and your surroundings
  • Mobility: Customise how you control and navigate your device
  • Speech: Express yourself your way
  • Cognitive: Stay focused and in control
  • Personalisation: Make it yours
  • Organisation: Remember what matters
  • Health: Access helpful health information
  • Safety: Put your mind at ease
  • Communication: Stay in touch

Taking the Vision category as an example, it includes features such as enlarging text, switching to bold text, inverting colours, applying colour filters, reducing transparency, increasing contrast, and reducing motion. Some features — such as Sound Recognition — received a big push from Apple when they launched, but still aren't widely understood by the general public.

Sound Recognition can detect specific sounds and send you a notification via on-device intelligence when it picks them up. It can recognise 15 different sounds — and you can also train your device to recognise your own name, as well as distinctive electronic sounds in your environment, such as beeps from kitchen appliances, certain types of alarm, or doorbell chimes. On HomePod, Sound Recognition can also pick up smoke or carbon monoxide alarms. Sound Recognition works with CarPlay too. Your iPhone will detect sirens, car horns, and even a crying baby. If you're using CarPlay, a notification will pop up on your car's display when a specific sound is detected.

The page is a comprehensive showcase of the accessibility features currently available across Apple's device lineup, and it's genuinely impressive. Each subcategory offers individual instructions for every supported device, covering — depending on the feature — iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Vision Pro, and CarPlay.
